title: Approximation of an effective object with prescribed jet and associated graded ring
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme]: every base morphism admits cartesian pullbacks and every fibre is a groupoid. Assume it preserves directed affine limits on objects, meaning that every object over the limit of a small directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes is isomorphic to a pullback from some stage. Let $(C,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra with residue field $k=C/\mathfrak m$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; local means having a unique maximal ideal and complete means $C\cong\varprojlim_{n\geq1} C/\mathfrak m^n$. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}k\to S$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $s$ be its image, and suppose $R_s$ is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. For every $x_C\in\mathcal X(C)$ and integer $N\geq1$ there exist a finitely generated commutative $R$-algebra $A$, a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n\subset A$, an object $y\in\mathcal X(A)$, an $R$-algebra isomorphism $e_N:C/\mathfrak m^N\xrightarrow{\sim}A/\mathfrak n^N$, and an isomorphism between $x_C|_{C/\mathfrak m^N}$ and $y|_{A/\mathfrak n^N}$ over $e_N$. Here finitely generated means generated by finitely many elements as an $R$-algebra. Moreover there is an isomorphism of graded $k$-algebras $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}(C)\cong\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}(A)$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring], where $A/\mathfrak n$ is identified with $k$ through the residue-field isomorphism induced by $e_N$.

proof.text: Order the finitely generated $R$-subalgebras $D_i\subset C$ by inclusion. This is a small directed set: the algebra generated by the union of two finite generating sets is an upper bound. Their union is $C$, and the union is a ring colimit since compatible maps agree on overlaps and hence define a unique map on the union. The affine-limit comparison identifies $\operatorname{Spec}C$ with the inverse limit of the $\operatorname{Spec}D_i$. The assumed preservation of these limits on objects therefore supplies some $D=D_i$, an object $z\in\mathcal X(D)$, and $z|_C\cong x_C$. Write $D=R[y_1,\ldots,y_u]/(f_1,\ldots,f_v)$ using finite presentation over the Noetherian base, and let $\bar a_i\in C$ be the images of $y_i$.

Because $k$ is a finite type $R$-algebra, choose finitely many algebra generators of $k$ and lift them to $C$. Adjoin to these lifts generators of the ideal $\mathfrak m$, which exist by Noetherianity. This gives $T=R[x_1,\ldots,x_w]\to C$ whose reduction $T\to k$ is surjective. Its kernel $\mathfrak p$ is maximal. The induced map $T\to C/\mathfrak m^2$ is surjective: lift the residue of an element, then express the remaining element modulo $\mathfrak m^2$ as a linear combination of the chosen ideal generators with residue coefficients lifted from $T$. Put $U=T_{\mathfrak p}$ and $P=\widehat U$, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak pP$. The cited Noetherianity, localization, completion and finite-level comparison statements show that $U,P$ are Noetherian and that $P/\mathfrak q^j=U/(\mathfrak pU)^j$. The local map $U\to C$ extends to $P\to C$ by applying it on each quotient and taking compatible coordinates in $C=\varprojlim C/\mathfrak m^j$. It has residue field $k$ and is surjective on cotangent spaces by the preceding surjectivity modulo $\mathfrak m^2$. Thus the surjectivity clause of complete-local cotangent rigidity gives a surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow C$.

Choose lifts $a_i\in P$ of $\bar a_i$. The kernel of $P\twoheadrightarrow C$ is finitely generated, say by $b_1,\ldots,b_r$. Each $f_j(a)$ belongs to that kernel, so choose $c_{ji}\in P$ with $f_j(a)=\sum_i c_{ji}b_i$. The kernel of the row $b:P^r\to P$ is a submodule of a finite module over the Noetherian ring $P$, and is therefore finite. Choose generators as columns of a matrix $K:P^t\to P^r$. Then $\operatorname{im}K=\ker b$ and $bK=0$. Apply initial-ideal stability to $(P,\mathfrak q,b,K)$ to obtain $h$. Fix $M\geq\max(N,h,2)$. This increase of precision will later be reduced back to the requested $N$.

The contraction of $\mathfrak p$ to $R$ is the prime $s$. The ring $R_s[x_1,\ldots,x_w]$ is a G-ring by the finite type theorem applied to the hypothesized G-ring $R_s$. Localizing it at the prime determined by $\mathfrak p$ gives $U$, which is still a G-ring directly from the definition: each of its prime localizations is the corresponding prime localization of the original G-ring, with the same completion map. Apply étale Artin approximation with ambient ring $T$, prime $\mathfrak p$, and the finite system of polynomial equations in the variables $a_i,b_i,c_{ji},K_{i\ell}$ given by $$f_j(a)-\sum_i c_{ji}b_i=0,\qquad \sum_i b_iK_{i\ell}=0.$$ Its formal solution lies in $P=\widehat{T_{\mathfrak p}}$. Obtain an étale $T$-algebra $B$, a prime $\mathfrak v$ over $\mathfrak p$ with residue field $k$, and a solution $(a^{\prime},b^{\prime},c^{\prime},K^{\prime})$ agreeing modulo the $M$th maximal-ideal power in the completed local ring. By the standard étale neighbourhood theorem, replace $B$ by $B_g$ for some $g\notin\mathfrak v$ so that it is a standard étale $T$-algebra, explicitly $T[t,Y]/(F,YH-1)$. This keeps the solution, the chosen local ring and its completion, and makes finite presentation over $T$ explicit.

We spell out the common completion used for the congruences. Apply the étale-completion comparison statement to $S=X=Y=\operatorname{Spec}T$, $U_{\rm sch}=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $p:\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}T$, and $f=p$, at $\mathfrak v$ over $\mathfrak p$. Its formal isomorphism $\varphi$ is the identity of $P$; its congruence assumption is the equality $g=\widehat p^{\sharp}$, so holds identically for every precision. It follows that $\widehat{B_{\mathfrak v}}$ is canonically $P$ as a $T$-algebra. Interpret all primed entries there. They differ from the original entries in $\mathfrak q^M$. In particular $b_i^{\prime}\in\mathfrak q$, since $b_i\in\ker(P\to C)\subset\mathfrak q$. The displayed standard presentation makes $B$ finite type over $T$, hence over $R$; so is $A=B/(b_1^{\prime},\ldots,b_r^{\prime})$. These rings are Noetherian by the finite type algebra theorem. The residue map $B\to\kappa(\mathfrak v)=k$ is surjective: its image contains the surjective image of $T\to k$. Hence $\mathfrak v$ is maximal, contains the $b_i^{\prime}$, and induces a maximal ideal $\mathfrak n$ of $A$.

The equations $f_j(a^{\prime})=\sum_i c_{ji}^{\prime}b_i^{\prime}$ define an $R$-algebra map $D\to A$, $y_i\mapsto a_i^{\prime}$; define $y=z|_A$. Put $J=(b_i)\subset P$ and $J^{\prime}=(b_i^{\prime})\subset P$. Since $b_i-b_i^{\prime}\in\mathfrak q^M$, $$J+\mathfrak q^M=J^{\prime}+\mathfrak q^M.$$ Completion modulo powers, and localization at the unique maximal ideal of $B/\mathfrak v^j$, give $B/\mathfrak v^j\cong P/\mathfrak q^j$ for $j\geq1$. Indeed a ring modulo a power of a maximal ideal has just that maximal ideal, so every element outside it is already a unit. Taking quotients by the images of $b_i^{\prime}$ therefore gives $$A/\mathfrak n^M\cong P/(J^{\prime}+\mathfrak q^M)=P/(J+\mathfrak q^M)\cong C/\mathfrak m^M.$$ The maps from $D$ agree in this common quotient because $a_i-a_i^{\prime}\in\mathfrak q^M$. Pullback functoriality in the fibred groupoid identifies the two restricted objects there. Reducing to the $N$th power of their maximal ideals gives $e_N$ in the stated direction and the required object isomorphism.

Apply initial-ideal stability to the two rows and matrices in $P$. The original complex is exact at $P^r$, the perturbed maps compose to zero by the equations just solved, and $M\geq h$. Thus for every $d\geq0$ the denominators $$\mathfrak q^{d+1}+(J\cap\mathfrak q^d)=\mathfrak q^{d+1}+(J^{\prime}\cap\mathfrak q^d)$$ coincide. The degree-$d$ graded piece of $P/J$ is the quotient of $\mathfrak q^d$ by the left denominator, and that of $P/J^{\prime}$ is the quotient by the right denominator. Identity on representatives induces the comparison in every degree. These comparisons preserve multiplication: the classes of $u\in\mathfrak q^d$ and $v\in\mathfrak q^e$ multiply to the class of $uv$ on both sides. They preserve the unit and the residue-field action for the same reason. Their direct sum is consequently an isomorphism of graded $k$-algebras. Here $P/J=C$, and the finite-level completion comparisons give $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak n}(A)=\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak q}(P/J^{\prime})$, since their maps on every power quotient are induced by the same map $B\to P$. In degree zero this comparison is the residue identification from the common $M$th quotient, hence from $e_N$. This proves the final clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NO-b330606bd (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery against Stacks 07XB (artin.tex) and 07VE/07VF (more-algebra.tex). The item statement is unchanged from the base and faithfully gives the affine-base case of 07XB, conclusions (1)-(6). The item is unsplit in live and side-live, there is no repair note, and nothing supersedes it. Steps 1-7 are all correct. Step 1: descent to a finitely generated D via 01YW and 00FP. Step 2: P = completion of T_p, which surjects onto C by the surjectivity clause of the rigidity node; its hypotheses all hold. Step 3: finite kernel, matrix K and h from the new node. Step 4: U is a G-ring from 07PV plus the definition, so 0CAR applies to T at p; 00UE then gives a standard étale presentation. Step 5: the 0CAV congruence node with f = p and φ = id identifies the completion of B_v with P; v is maximal because T → k is surjective. Step 6: B/v^j = P/q^j and J + q^M = J' + q^M give A/n^M ≅ C/m^M, the map from D and the object isomorphism. Step 7: equal initial denominators give an identity-on-representatives graded ring isomorphism, using the modular law and A/n^j = P/(J' + q^j) for every j. New node lem-sfb-adic-relation-matrix-initial-ideals: exactly 07VE+07VF with N = P, I = q and h = c+1. It is true; I tested empty and zero matrices, a field, k[[x]], and the Koszul case on (x,y); a perturbation with no compatible K' shows the hypothesis b'K' = 0 is needed. It is self-contained and not a duplicate: rg -L for 07VE, 07VF and approximate-complex finds nothing else, and the existing Artin-Rees nodes are only intersection bounds. It restates no clause of the item, and its Mathlib searches are recorded. I accept the four declared tool_uses (0CAR, 0CAV-congruence, 0316, 07PV) as generic commutative algebra. Batch-5 flags: lem-trf-artin-approximation-etale-local-map, lem-trf-etale-completion-congruence and the rigidity node's link to lem-trf-vector-space-quotient-dimension are generic algebra or linear algebra.
